dimensions.assessment: Affects American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries receiving emergency medical services outside the IHS, excluding elderly or disabled individuals.
dimensions.evidence: This bill does not apply to individuals who are elderly or disabled, who continue to have a 30-day notification requirement for emergency services.

dimensions.assessment: Lengthens the notification period from 72 hours to at least 15 days, reducing the risk of claim rejections for untimely notice.
dimensions.evidence: extends from 72 hours to not less than 15 days the time period to notify the Purchased/Referred Care (PRC) program

dimensions.assessment: May affect federal claim payouts under the PRC program, but no precise fiscal figures are provided.
Amends Section 406 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act to alter emergency service notification timelines.
dimensions.evidence: Section 406 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act (25 U.S.C. 1646) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change to notification rules.

missing_information: Specific budgetary impact or expected change in federal outlays.
importance_detail.rationale: H.R. 8658 extends the time period to notify the Purchased/Referred Care program of emergency medical care from non-IHS providers to not less than 15 days, excluding elderly or disabled individuals.
